findings.title: Post-worker retention/finalization failure strands reserved peers
findings.trigger: put_json(report) fails after the worker ran, or any registry.finish raises during the sequential member loop. Neither operation is inside a cleanup/finalization guard. Reservation rollback lines66-69 similarly stops at the first finish failure.
findings.consequence: Some or all families remain running despite a completed physical execution; later attempts see reservation charges rather than retained observed use, and no summary is written.
findings.suggested_correction: Persist a durable shared-execution lifecycle and completion payload before per-family finalization, then finalize each member independently and retain all errors. Provide idempotent reconciliation of already-finished versus running members without launching another worker. On unknown resource use charge reservations rather than zero; zero is valid only for proven never-launched rollback.

findings.title: Supervisor termination has no recoverable worker lifecycle
findings.trigger: SIGTERM to supervisor uses default termination, bypassing the BaseException handler. The worker has its own session and may continue. After any supervisor loss the durable registry contains starts/config but no launch PID/group, launched state, resource result or recovery procedure.
findings.consequence: An active or finished worker can outlive its supervisor with family attempts stranded and no complete failure evidence. A retry can create a new shared_id/trial because TrialRegistry.start only bars a running attempt of the same trial.
findings.suggested_correction: Install termination handling to kill/reap the worker and write interrupted outcomes. Persist launch/group and shared completion state, and reject/reconcile any unresolved shared execution for these families before creating a new UUID trial. Handle hard crashes with explicit durable recovery rather than assuming cleanup ran.

findings.title: Recorder trusts mutable summary members/resources without validating trial completion
findings.trigger: Edit summary.members to other/nonexistent attempt/trial IDs while keeping the same family keys, or edit resource totals. Checks compare shared_id and verification only; member identity and telemetry are taken from summary, not immutable supervised.members/resources. TrialRegistry.state is never checked.
findings.consequence: Case evidence can falsely identify another attempt or wrong resource costs, and can attach even when family finalization never succeeded. This breaks the shared physical execution/accounting proof.
findings.suggested_correction: Use immutable supervised members/resources as authority; require exact wrapper equality for those fields and reject duplicate family entries before dictionary construction. Verify each registry attempt is succeeded, belongs to its stated trial/family, has matching shared configuration/code/golden, actual charges, and this supervised artifact in result_artifacts. Verify frozen family registrations again on attachment.

findings.title: Supervisor permits incomplete participating family sets
findings.trigger: Invoke with only the F08 registration, or any proper subset of the three. It passes distinct/nonempty validation then runs all tests, including all F05-F08 changes, while reserving and charging only supplied families. Recorder later rejects the family set but the physical execution already occurred.
findings.consequence: The same combined dependent code can run outside omitted families budgets; attachment validation cannot repair the already-unaccounted execution.
findings.suggested_correction: Require exactly the three frozen family identities before reservations and execution. Check their full registered budgets/limits and detect unresolved shared attempts as one group.

findings.title: Complete review and exact case mappings are not frozen or checked before execution
findings.trigger: Supervisor retains an arbitrary MD review file but does not inspect the batch-review JSON flags or coverage documents. Those reports and recording script are excluded from code_manifest. Recorder later accepts whichever coverage modules/methods and review JSON exist at attachment. A coverage map or review claim can therefore change after the actual run without changing snapshot.
findings.consequence: The execution is not bound to the complete-reviewed/single-repair evidence or exact source-case mapping it later claims. test_modules can also be switched to unrelated passed modules, since allowed family modules are supplied only by mutable coverage.
findings.suggested_correction: Before reservations, validate and retain the completed review/repair record, all three coverage mappings and recording script; pin their references into shared configuration. Validate source case sets, explicit remaining lists, approved per-family modules and method identity against static source. Recorder should consume those immutable artifacts and bind reviewed/repaired code identities to actual snapshot. Existing missing F06/F07 coverage at review time is a readiness gate, not an excuse to run.

findings.title: Killed or crashed worker loses accumulated assertion output
findings.trigger: verify.run stores unittest output in io.StringIO and only publishes its report after the entire suite and traceability work finish. CPU/wall kill, MemoryError or unexpected exception before result creation leaves supervisor stdout without the completed assertion log. Temporary result directory is removed.
findings.consequence: Failure report retains return code/resources but cannot preserve full assertion progress/output for a partially executed failed attempt as the frozen protocols require.
findings.suggested_correction: Use a worker mode that streams/tees assertion events and stdout/stderr to supervisor-retained files as work occurs; capture partial result bytes even if JSON is incomplete. Preserve tracebacks and partial assertion identities on exceptional exit. Retain and hash the exact worker source used.

findings.title: Read-then-write evidence merge can drop concurrent ledger additions
findings.trigger: Recorder reads ledger.current before constructing all family artifacts and copies existing artifact/assertion lists. Another authorized updater appends evidence to an affected owner before ledger.update. update locks and reads current state, but replaces list fields with the stale recorder lists.
findings.consequence: The single ledger transaction is atomic across owners yet can erase newer evidence attachments from current state.
findings.suggested_correction: Perform union/merge against current owner records under the ledger lock, or introduce an expected-head/expected-owner-version compare-and-swap and retry assembly on conflict. Keep all-owner attachment as one ledger transaction.

findings.title: Attachment can commit before known audit/summary failures with no idempotent recovery
findings.trigger: ledger.update commits before reading current-checkpoint/conformance files and before ledger.audit(scope). A missing/corrupt report or stale scope produces failure after attachment; rerun creates new timestamped report artifacts and another transaction. Mutable coverage reports are also written before ledger commit.
findings.consequence: A caller sees failed recording despite durable attachment, and retries proliferate different evidence artifacts without a shared-execution attachment receipt; dashboard reports can disagree.
findings.suggested_correction: Preflight scope audit and all required inputs before commit; make shared_execution_id plus immutable mapping/snapshot identities an idempotent attachment key. Persist a committed attachment receipt with transaction ID and regenerate dashboard files atomically from it; distinguish postcommit presentation failure from failed ledger attachment.

positive_checks: One Popen worker produces one UUID shared_execution_id; same observed worker CPU/wall/RSS is charged to each supplied member and not presented as summed physical use.

Protocol/golden bytes are checked against immutable registration artifacts and family protocol before reservations. Full code snapshot includes recursive src/tests/references Python, config/golden JSON and pyproject/lock bytes.

Recorder recursively traverses nested exact ArtifactRef envelopes with hash-verified reads and content-addressed copies; supplied source-case capsules expose retained_preparation_files refs and all three case keys match actual registered capsule schema.

Every prepared case ID must occur exactly once; mapped short method names must resolve to exactly one actually passed full method ID within declared modules; evidence keeps whole_case_verified false. F08-26 empty methods with remaining gates is intentional.
Ledger.update validates all owner records then atomically appends one all-owner evidence transaction; artifact publication before attachment does not partially update owner records.
readiness_limits: reports/f06-f07-implementation-coverage.json did not exist during this review; parent is still reviewing/finalizing that family. The tools should validate all coverage artifacts before running.
Batch review artifacts are still to be assembled; review findings concern missing pre-run gates, not their eventual contents.
No claim of complete recursive closure of every historical source graph: this static review checked traversal implementation and the three capsule envelopes, without executing the recorder.
next_step: Root combines these findings with full implementation reviews in the one consolidated repair pass; do not execute either orchestration tool before repair and review record freeze.
